extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, researchers and practitioners interested in the European Investment Bank and EU development/finance
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional overview of the European Investment Bank (EIB), describing its objectives, areas of activity, eligibility and screening criteria, governance, accountability mechanisms, transparency rules, and instruments (loans, guarantees, intermediated SME finance, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The bank funds projects in the areas of; climate, environment, innovation and skills, infrastructure, small and medium-sized enterprises, cohesion and development as well as crises including the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIB aims to support sustainable economic growth within member states and externally and is part of the European Commission's Investment Plan for Europe which aims to bridge investment gaps by taking on some project risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project eligibility criteria (geographic / public interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: It funds projects both inside and outside the EU that meet one of the criteria of; in less developed regions, where projects can not be funded by individual member states and projects which benefit multiple member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 1959 the Bank has signed nearly 25,000 projects worldwide; eligibility emphasizes development impact and cross‑member or underserved-region benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary screening requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project financing is granted after preliminary screenings of the viability and the carbon emissions associated with the projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening includes viability assessment and carbon-emissions considerations as part of project appraisal before financing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate alignment / Paris Agreement commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIB Group committed in November 2019 to align its activities with the goals and principles of the Paris Agreement by the end of 2020 and approved the EIB Group Climate Bank Roadmap 2021–2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roadmap actions include stopping financing of fossil fuel projects, supporting a just transition, increasing accountability, and accelerating green funding contributions to EU climate goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy project CO2 threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: It will only fund energy projects capable of producing one kilowatt hour of energy for less than 250 grams of carbon dioxide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric threshold is used as an explicit eligibility filter for energy investments; the policy change received commentary about its scope and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to stop fossil fuel financing
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of 2021, the EIB will stop financing all fossil fuel projects (as stated in the Roadmap and related announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents a sectoral exclusion/policy shift intended to reorient financing toward low‑carbon and renewable energy projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pan‑European Guarantee Fund (COVID response) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: European Union companies are eligible to seek financing from the Pan‑European Guarantee Fund if they have financial issues due to the economic implication of the COVID‑19 pandemic but could have been able to secure loans under pre‑crisis circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIB Board approved a €25 billion fund aimed to mobilise up to €200 billion of additional private sector financing for SMEs and mid‑caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME and mid‑cap financing approach and size definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Through intermediaries, the EIB finances micro‑enterprises (0–9 employees), small enterprises (10–49 employees), medium‑sized enterprises (50–249 employees), mid‑caps (250–3,000 employees). The EIB Group provides direct financing to mid‑caps and offers venture debt financing under specific facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EIB works via a broad network of commercial and national promotional banks, leasing companies, venture capital and private equity funds and other service providers to reach firms in regions with limited access to finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and skills investment objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Support targeted at the development and commercialisation of new products, economic processes and business models, increased investment in research and development, education, upskilling and training and improved connectivity and access through broadband and mobile networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes adoption/diffusion of digital and emerging technologies and empowering women's participation in the labour market; historical investment totals cited (e.g., €14.4 billion in 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion financing target
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIB's annual target for cohesion financing is 30% of all new operations in the EU, Pre‑Accession and EFTA countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This target is used to prioritise projects addressing inequalities by providing jobs, education, public infrastructure and services, and sustainable environments across the EU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency policy and publication exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The bank publishes documents related to its role, governance, accountability, policies and operations but, as part of the Transparency policy, the EIB does not publish information that may harm legitimate interests of clients and project partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of withheld information include personal data, commercial interests such as patents, and information related to on‑going investigations; a public register was set up in 2014 to increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints Mechanism admissibility and remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints can range from environmental degradation or threats to community health and safety to involuntary resettlement. The Complaints Mechanism examines whether the EIB Group has failed to comply with internal policies, standards or procedures or with applicable legislation and offers mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mechanism monitors closed complaints to ensure agreed measures are implemented and feeds identified improvements to senior management; it also organises events to inform public and CSOs about admissibility and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Procurements Complaints Committee remit
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIB's Project Procurements Complaints Committee (PCC) deals with project procurement complaints, e.g. objections arising from tendering of EIB‑financed contracts for goods, works and consultant services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCC provides a structured channel for procurement‑related grievances in financed projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud Investigations Division functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fraud Investigations Division investigates allegations, verifies the existence of a robust anti‑fraud policy framework, proactively identifies actual or potential vulnerabilities and trains staff on fraud awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the EIB's internal control architecture alongside the Anti‑fraud Policy and other governance instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control and governance bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal and independent controls include Investigations, Audit Committee, Compliance, Credit Risk, Financial Control, Internal Control, Internal Audit, External Auditors, and Operations Evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bodies prepare/appraise/finance projects, assess/manage risks, run studies and raise resources; they aim to guarantee integrity and soundness of EIB operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Committee duties and appointment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit committee functions as an independent control body and verifies the bank's operations and the validity of its accounts. Its six independent members are appointed for a non‑renewable term of office of six consecutive financial years by the board of governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee issues a report on the bank's financial statements at the time of approval by the board of directors, appoints external auditors and evaluates their independence, and reports directly to the board of governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with external control bodies and citizen recourse
rubrics_metrics.description: The bank cooperates with the European Court of Auditors, the European Anti‑Fraud Office (OLAF) and the European Ombudsman. According to Article 287(3) TFEU, the European Court of Auditors has access to information required for audit of EU expenditure and revenue managed by the EIB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on a memorandum of understanding with the European Ombudsman, EU citizens can escalate concerns regarding an EIB project, policy or activity to the Ombudsman if the outcome of the EIB's Complaints Mechanism is not satisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandates governing operations (EIF/EIB mandates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIF operates on the basis of specific mandates from the European Council and the European Parliament, from the European Commission or other public authorities, from the European Investment Bank or at its own risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EIB Group activities can be mandate‑driven (EU mandates) or undertaken at the institution's own risk, affecting scope, oversight and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and Social Standards and governance policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIB has Environmental and Social Standards, an Anti‑fraud Policy, and an EIB Group Policy towards weakly regulated, non‑transparent and non‑cooperative jurisdictions and tax good governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments are referenced in accountability and transparency debates (e.g., in responses to tax avoidance and corporate governance concerns) and are part of continuous procedural improvements.
